name: Should I install a structural beam for an open layout or keep a half-wall instead?

mainEntity.name: Should I install a structural beam for an open layout or keep a half-wall instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners should choose an engineered support beam when they need to remove an entire load-bearing wall, but a partial wall or pass-through opening is better when keeping some separation or utility runs. A full beam opens up the floor plan completely, improving sightlines and natural light between kitchens and living areas, but it requires temporary shoring and structural modifications. A pass-through or half-wall (knee wall) offers a practical tradeoff: it creates an open, connected feel while preserving wall space for electrical outlets, plumbing, base cabinetry, or kitchen island placement without requiring full-span beam reconstruction.
acceptedAnswer.description: A structural beam provides a completely open floor plan, whereas a half-wall retains electrical and plumbing runs while still enhancing light and sightlines.
